# mdpdf

mdpdf is a command-line tool that converts Markdown files into PDFs. Give it a Markdown document and it gives you back a PDF that's ready to share, print or archive. You don't need a browser engine, a LaTeX install or a long list of setup steps.

mdpdf is written in Go and ships as a single 8 MB binary. To install it, download the binary, put it on your `PATH` and start converting. Because it's one self-contained file, it works the same on your laptop, in a CI pipeline or inside a small container image.

mdpdf is also fast: it renders 100 pages in 1.2 seconds. That makes it practical for large documentation sets, automated report generation and build steps where you don't want PDF conversion to slow things down. You can regenerate documents as often as you need.

Use mdpdf when you want a lightweight way to produce PDFs from the Markdown you already write. It's easy to script and easy to add to the tools you already use.

mdpdf is open source and released under the MIT License. You're free to use, modify and distribute it in personal and commercial projects. Contributions, bug reports and feature requests are welcome.
